{"type":"chore","title":"chore(automouse): give post-plan exactly MAX_ATTEMPTS runs","commit_subject":"chore(automouse): seed .attempts=1 at handoff; add P4 cap regression","summary_md":"## Summary\n\n- Before this change, a plan whose impl succeeded but whose post-plan kept failing got `MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1 = 4` post-plan runs. The impl handoff cleared `.attempts`, so the next claim started the counter fresh at 1, 2, 3 — and the cap fired one run too late.\n- Fix: at handoff creation, write `1` to `.attempts` instead of removing it. The impl run's post-plan is attempt 1. Subsequent claims increment normally, and the cap fires at exactly `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` total post-plan runs.\n- Impl's own failed-attempt history is replaced by the 1, so it never eats the post-plan budget.\n- A held PR is a success — the loop-side check files it to `done/` before any attempts are burned.\n- README updated to reflect the new handoff semantics.\n\n## Test changes\n\n- **P1** — `assert_absent` on `.attempts` now proves `refund_attempt` ran (seeded to 1, refund removes it), not just that impl cleared it.\n- **P2** — assertion flipped from `assert_absent` (counter absent) to `assert_eq ... 1` (counter present, seeded to 1) after a genuine post-plan failure.\n- **P4 (new)** — resumes `ppslow` three times after P2's state. Checks that `.attempts` increments 2 → 3, that the plan stays in `queue/` through resume 2, and that the third resume files it to `skipped/` with exactly `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` total post-plan invocations.\n\n## Corpus diff\n\nMeasured 2026-10-03 over all automouse logs:\n\n```\nplans_with_postplan=807\nold_rule_cap4_reached=22\nnew_rule_cap3_reached=50\npostplan_runs_avoided_under_cap3=28\n```\n\nCounts are upper bounds. A plan whose last post-plan run succeeded reached the cap without being skipped, and env-breaker refunds let a few plans run 5 to 7 times.\n\nCloses a-jay85/IBL5-backlog#1300"}
